svg.title: Turbo: Spend, record, approve
svg.desc: Draft guide to purchase orders, expenses, time sheets, and approval amounts. Three separate workflows and a guide to PO requirements. Amounts shown as examples are not live company settings.

text.tspan: POs authorise purchases. Expenses record costs. Time sheets record work.
THREE PATHS. EACH HAS ITS OWN APPROVAL.
Check whether a PO is required. Use the guide below.
Turbo can combine approval steps when policy allows. A PO alone does not record the actual expense.
OPEN THE ACTIVE PO → CREATE ITS EXPENSE
Supplier invoice, corporate Visa purchase, out-of-pocket expense, allowance or mileage.
or reject it with a reason.
This is separate from the PO.
Rejected expense? Recall, correct and resubmit. Foreign-currency expenses need settlement before commit.
Use time entries for work hours. A PO is not part of the time-sheet approval path.
Submit them as a time sheet
Rejected time sheet? Recall, correct and resubmit. Required project authorisation must be approved before submission.
A / WHEN A PO IS REQUIRED
With a job → PO at any amount.
Without a job → PO at or above
Confirm the live setting before use.
limit must cover the approval total.
$0 means no authority in that category.
Mileage, Fuel Card, Allowance and enabled Personal Reimbursement entries do not require a PO.
Payables administrators can bypass the amount limit for On Account entries; the job rule still applies.
A job links time, expenses and POs to the same project. A corporate card is a payment type, not an approval exemption.
Draft based on current application rules · Amount examples are not live settings · Commit does not mean paid
